report: Live Bot vs Backtest Bot Alignment Analysis
summary: The backtest has TWO run methods: run() (copy of live) and run_backtest() (simplified M15 stepper). run_backtest() is the one actually used and has significant behavioral differences from the live run() loop.

critical_misalignments.area: run_backtest() vs run() - completely different implementations
critical_misalignments.description: run_backtest() is a simplified M15 bar stepper that does NOT use most of the methods from run(). The run() in backtest is a near-copy of live but is NEVER CALLED during backtesting.
critical_misalignments.impact: Backtest results may not reflect live trading behavior accurately

critical_misalignments.backtest_behavior: run_backtest() skips weekends entirely with 'if weekday >= 5: continue'. No Friday position closing, no order pausing, no Monday resume.
critical_misalignments.impact: Backtest never experiences weekend gap risk or forced Friday closes. Positions carry through weekends without the half-lot size reduction that live bot applies.

critical_misalignments.area: Spread queue never checked in run_backtest()
critical_misalignments.backtest_behavior: run_backtest() never calls check_awaiting_spread_signals(). Setups added to spread queue are lost.
critical_misalignments.impact: Trades that would be placed after spread improves are never placed in backtest. Understates trade count.

critical_misalignments.area: Limit order compounding missing from run_backtest()
critical_misalignments.backtest_behavior: run_backtest() never updates lot sizes on pending orders
critical_misalignments.impact: Pending orders in backtest use original lot size, not compounded. Minor impact unless equity changes significantly before fill.

critical_misalignments.area: DDD/TDD monitoring uses local vars vs challenge_manager
critical_misalignments.live_behavior: run() uses self.monitor_5ers_drawdown(), self.execute_protection_actions(), DDD protection loop thread, and challenge_manager
critical_misalignments.backtest_behavior: run_backtest() uses local day_start_equity, trading_halted_today vars with inline TDD/DDD checks
critical_misalignments.impact: Different DDD calculation method. Live uses challenge_manager.day_start_equity (synced at midnight), backtest uses local var reset each new day. Functionally similar but not identical code paths.

critical_misalignments.live_behavior: DDD protection loop has graduated tiers: warn at 2.0%, reduce risk at 3.0%, halt at 3.5%
critical_misalignments.backtest_behavior: run_backtest() only halts at 3.5% (no graduated response)
critical_misalignments.impact: Backtest doesn't reduce risk at 3.0% DDD like live does. May take larger positions than live would in drawdown scenarios.

critical_misalignments.area: News blackout not checked in run_backtest()
critical_misalignments.live_behavior: is_news_blackout() checked before placing orders (blocks order placement during high-impact news)
critical_misalignments.backtest_behavior: No news blackout check in run_backtest() loop
critical_misalignments.impact: Backtest places orders during news events that live bot would skip. May overstate trade count.

critical_misalignments.live_behavior: Separate _do_midnight_equity_sync() at 00:00 with manual override support, DDD reset at midnight
critical_misalignments.backtest_behavior: run_backtest() resets day_start_equity inline at each new day. Simpler but functionally equivalent.
critical_misalignments.impact: Minimal - both use MAX(equity, balance) for new day start

expected_differences.reason: These handle live MT5 state management that doesn't apply to simulation
Backtest needs to pass simulated time instead of using datetime.now()

recommendations: HIGH: Add check_awaiting_spread_signals() calls to run_backtest() entry queue section
MEDIUM: Add graduated DDD response (risk reduction at 3.0%) to run_backtest()
LOW: Consider adding simplified Friday close logic to run_backtest() for realistic weekend gap modeling
LOW: Add news blackout simulation using historical news calendar data
